ip-lookup.title: IP Lookup
ip-lookup.description: Look up your public IP and the geolocation/ISP of any IP (requires network, via free public services)
ip-lookup.networkNote: This tool needs the network: geolocation comes from ipwho.is, and “Get my public IP” requests api64.ipify.org, api.ipify.org, ipv4.icanhazip.com and ipinfo.io until one succeeds. Those third-party services see your IP and User-Agent.
ip-lookup.onlineNote: Geolocation results are for reference only

dns-lookup.title: DNS Lookup
dns-lookup.description: Query A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA/SRV/CAA records at once, with TTL, multi-resolver comparison and record diagnostics (requires network)
dns-lookup.compareNote: Only record values are compared: public resolvers cache at different times, so TTL gaps are not a mismatch
dns-lookup.networkNote: This tool needs the network: queries go straight to the public DoH resolver you pick, which sees the domain and record types you look up. Cloudflare and Google are usually unreachable from mainland China.
dns-lookup.onlineNote: Answers come from public recursive DNS caches and are for reference only; your local ISP may resolve differently.

errors.invalid: Not a valid hostname — use something like example.com

states.unreachable: This resolver is unreachable from the current network — pick another one
states.nxdomainNotice: {{domain}} does not exist (NXDOMAIN), so no record type can return anything

typeHint.TXT: text, used for SPF and domain validation

A.name: A record (Address)
A.description: Maps a name to an IPv4 address — the most common record type. Example: example.com points at 1.1.1.1.

AAAA.name: AAAA record (IPv6 Address)
AAAA.description: Maps a name to an IPv6 address, e.g. example.com points at 2001:db8::1.

CNAME.name: CNAME record (Canonical Name)
CNAME.description: An alias that points one name at another, e.g. www at example.com; the resolver then looks up the target name.

MX.name: MX record (Mail Exchange)
MX.description: Names the servers that accept mail for the domain, each with a priority (lower wins) and a host name.

TXT.name: TXT record (Text)
TXT.description: Free-form text: SPF anti-spam policy, DKIM public keys and domain ownership proofs for console/vendor verification.

NS.name: NS record (Name Server)
NS.description: Delegates a zone: lists the authoritative DNS servers that answer for the domain or subdomain.

SOA.name: SOA record (Start of Authority)
SOA.description: One per zone: primary server, admin mailbox, serial number and the refresh/retry/expire timers replicas follow.

SRV.name: SRV record (Service Locator)
SRV.description: Publishes the host and port of a named service such as SIP or XMPP, with priority and weight.

CAA.name: CAA record (Certification Authority Authorization)
CAA.description: Restricts which CAs may issue TLS certificates for the domain, blocking mistaken or malicious issuance.

usage.name: Typical use cases
usage.description: Site migrations, load balancing, CDN onboarding, corporate mail setup, certificate issuance and ownership verification.

cnameConflict.title: CNAME coexists with other records at the same name
cnameConflict.detail: RFC 1034 §3.6.2: a name with a CNAME cannot also carry A/MX/TXT records — those get ignored. For a zone apex (@), use an A record or CNAME flattening.

mxNoAddress.title: MX target resolves to no address
mxNoAddress.detail: Mail delivery will fail; add an A or AAAA record for the hosts below.

spfMultiple.title: More than one v=spf1 record on the same host
spfMultiple.detail: RFC 7208 allows exactly one SPF record; several are a permanent error for the receiving side. Merge them.

spfTooManyLookups.title: SPF exceeds the DNS lookup limit
spfTooManyLookups.detail: RFC 7208 §4.6: include / a / mx / ptr / exists may trigger at most 10 lookups; beyond that the check fails outright.

noAddress.title: Neither an A nor an AAAA record
noAddress.detail: The host is not directly reachable. That is expected for mail-only or validation-only names.

noRecordsAtAll.title: This host has no records at all
noRecordsAtAll.detail: All nine types came back empty. If you queried a subdomain, double-check the host name or add a record in your DNS console.

caaMissing.title: No CAA record
caaMissing.detail: Any CA may issue for this domain. Add a CAA record if you want to restrict issuers.

caaPresent.title: Issuers allowed by CAA
caaPresent.detail: Only the listed CAs may issue certificates; check this first when issuance fails.
